title: Chiefs, Bengals Eye Colts’ Jonathan Taylor: Latest Trade Market Buzz for Star RB
body:
The Indianapolis Colts’ running back market has heated up as the NFL trade deadline approaches, with the Kansas City Chiefs and Cincinnati Bengals emerging as the most vocal suitors of former first‑overall pick Jonathan Taylor. While Indianapolis has yet to confirm an active pursuit of a deal, the buzz surrounding Taylor’s future has intensified after his modest performance against the Jacksonville Jaguars, prompting both teams to evaluate how a veteran back could reshape their offensive strategies heading into the postseason.

Taylor, who entered the league with lofty expectations after a record‑setting collegiate career at Alabama, has struggled to recapture his early‑year form this season. He entered the game against Jacksonville with 1,025 rushing yards and three touchdowns, but managed just 36 yards on 12 carries, a stark contrast to the 1,000‑plus yard seasons he posted in 2021 and 2022. The lackluster outing has amplified speculation that the Colts, who sit at 5‑6 and have already missed the playoffs, may be willing to move the former 2022 MVP in exchange for draft capital or a player who can fill the void left by his potential departure.

Kansas City, currently perched atop the AFC West with a 10‑2 record, has long been linked to a need for a reliable, power‑running complement to star quarterback Patrick Mahomes. The Chiefs’ offensive scheme, which thrives on play‑action and balanced attack, could benefit from a back capable of grinding out short gains and protecting Mahomes from blitzes. Sources close to the organization suggest that the Chiefs view Taylor as a low‑risk, high‑reward option: his experience and proven production when healthy could provide depth behind the versatile Isiah Pacheco, while also offering a contingency plan should injuries arise late in the season.

The Cincinnati Bengals, sitting at 8‑5 and fighting for a wild‑card berth, have a more immediate need for a workhorse back. Their current ground game, led by rookie Tyler Goodson and veteran Joe Mixon, has been inconsistent, prompting head coach Zac Taylor to explore alternatives that can sustain drives against stout defenses in the AFC North. A veteran like Taylor, who has demonstrated the ability to shoulder a heavy workload, could be the missing piece to stabilize the Bengals’ offense and give them a more versatile attack as they eye a potential playoff push.

Colts general manager Chris Ballard remains cautious about any trade discussions. In a brief interview before the Jaguars matchup, he emphasized that Indianapolis is “still evaluating options” and has not entered formal negotiations. The team’s front office appears to be weighing the value of Taylor’s contract—approximately $13 million for the remainder of the season—against the potential return in draft picks or a player who can contribute immediately. With the deadline looming, the window for a substantial offer is narrowing, and any deal would likely need to satisfy both the financial considerations and the Colts’ desire to receive a meaningful asset rather than a nominal exchange.

Analysts point out that the market for running backs has shifted dramatically over the past decade, with teams often preferring to develop younger talent or allocate resources elsewhere. Yet Taylor’s pedigree and recent resurgence in the early part of the season keep him on the radar of clubs seeking a proven performer. If a trade materializes, it would signal a rare instance of a high‑profile, mid‑season running back move, underscoring the lingering value placed on a balanced offensive attack in a league increasingly dominated by the passing game.

Looking ahead, the next few days will be critical for all parties involved. Should the Chiefs or Bengals secure a trade, they would need to integrate Taylor quickly, adjusting playbooks and roster spots before the final regular‑season games. Conversely, if Indianapolis decides to retain him, the Colts will have to rely on Taylor to rediscover his form and help the team finish the year on a positive note. As the deadline draws near, the NFL landscape will watch closely to see whether Jonathan Taylor’s journey continues with the Colts or takes a new turn in Kansas City or Cincinnati, potentially reshaping the offensive fortunes of whichever franchise lands his talents.
